name: Mishawaka
lede: Mishawaka began with bog iron. In 1832 Alanson Hurd sent a prospector up the St. Joseph River to look for ore, and in 1833 he bought land at the rapids and built the St. Joseph Iron Works, the town's first name. By 1837 four little towns stood side by side, and in February 1838 the legislature joined them under one name, Mishawaka. The town became a city in 1899, and its mills made Dodge pulleys, Ball-Band rubber boots and the Simplex motor car.
facts: Founded
iron works and town platted, 1833; incorporated as the village of St. Joseph Iron Works, 1835; four towns united as Mishawaka by act of the legislature, February 17, 1838; city, 1899
Name

from the Potawatomi; Howard's 1907 county history notes that the name Mishawaka was in use while the town's official name was still St. Joseph Iron Works, and that William Barbee's plat was the first to carry it on record. The linguist Michael McCafferty reads it as a Potawatomi word meaning "at the firewood-tree land"; the older reading, "swift water" or "big rapids," is the one the city and museum give
The four towns
St. Joseph Iron Works, Barbee's plat, Fowler's Addition, and Indiana City, platted on the north bank by Joseph Battell and James and Grove Lawrence in June 1836
Industry

the iron works built what is said to be the first blast furnace in Indiana and made pig iron from 1834; Wallace Dodge's factory opened in 1878; the Mishawaka Woolen Company, incorporated in 1874, became Ball-Band and then Uniroyal, and closed in 1997
A fire
in 1872 a fire burned 49 buildings downtown, and the town then barred wood-frame buildings from the business district
County seat
no; the county seat of St. Joseph County is South Bend, four miles downriver
where: Deeds, probate and marriage records are kept by St. Joseph County in South Bend, the county seat. The Mishawaka-Penn-Harris Public Library holds its Local & Family History Collection at the downtown Mishawaka library, with St. Joseph County newspapers on microfilm from 1853, and runs the Mishawaka Memories digital archive. The Mishawaka Enterprise has been published since the 1850s; the South Bend Area Genealogical Society has indexed its legal notices, and the South Bend News-Times (1913–1938) is free on Chronicling America. The History Museum, 808 W. Washington St., South Bend, keeps the county's historical collections. Howard's History of St. Joseph County (1907) gives the town a full chapter.

name: Elkhart
lede: Elkhart stands where the Elkhart River runs into the St. Joseph. Dr. Havilah Beardsley laid out the town in 1832 on the point between the two rivers, beside an older settlement and post office called Pulaski. It became a town in 1858 and a city in 1875, and a hydraulic canal built around 1870 turned the river into factory power. In 1874 Charles G. Conn began making cornet mouthpieces here, and Elkhart became the nation's band-instrument town.
facts: Founded
platted by Havilah Beardsley, 1832; town, 1858; city, 1875
Name

Chapman's county history (1881) says Beardsley named the town Elkhart because the island at the meeting of the rivers was shaped so much like an elk's heart, and that the Pulaski post office later took the name. Scholars trace the name further back, to an elk's-heart place name recorded in French in the 1700s
Water power
"The hydraulic works of 1870 opened up a new era in the progress of the town," Chapman wrote in 1881; mills and factories lined the canal
Band instruments
C. G. Conn began making cornet mouthpieces in 1874, then brass instruments; Conn, Buescher, Selmer and others made Elkhart a national center of the trade
Medicine
Franklin Miles founded the Miles Medical Company here in 1884; it later made Alka-Seltzer
County seat
no; Goshen, ten miles up the Elkhart River, is the county seat of Elkhart County
where: Deeds, probate and marriage records are kept by Elkhart County at Goshen, the county seat. The Elkhart Public Library keeps its local history collection on the second floor of the downtown library, with city directories, a searchable obituary index, a photo archive shared with Indiana Memory, and the Elkhart Truth archive. The Elkhart County Historical Museum, 304 W. Vistula St., Bristol, has a research library of photographs, diaries, family records and plat maps (appointments recommended). Chapman's History of Elkhart County (1881) and Deahl's Twentieth Century History (1905) both give the city long chapters.

name: Goshen
lede: Goshen was made to be a county seat. In 1831 the Elkhart County commissioners chose the high ground on the Elkhart River as the most suitable point, ordered their agent Oliver Crane to lay out a town, and sold the first lots that July. It was incorporated as a town in 1854 and as a city in 1868. That same year a hydraulic canal, dug to carry the river's water past the mills, was finished, and Goshen became a mill and factory town around its courthouse square.
facts: Founded
laid out as the county seat, 1831; first lots sold July 1831; town, 1854; city, 1868
Name

Chapman's county history (1881) says Oliver Crane, who came from near Goshen, New York, gave the town its name; the Goshen Historical Society points to the Biblical Land of Goshen, a name for fertile ground
County seat
yes, of Elkhart County since 1831; the courthouse stands on the square downtown
Water power
the hydraulic canal, begun about 1866 and completed in 1868, drew water from the Elkhart River to run flour mills and factories, as Chapman described in 1881
A college
Goshen College, a Mennonite college, dates from 1894
where: Goshen is the county seat, so Elkhart County's deeds, probate, marriage and court records are kept here. The Goshen Public Library's Indiana Room has Goshen newspapers on microfilm from 1837 to 2022, Goshen city directories from 1883 (selected years), an obituary card file from 1970 and a Goshen News index from 2007. The Goshen Historical Society runs a museum at 124 S. Main St. The Elkhart County Historical Museum, 304 W. Vistula St., Bristol, has a research library with plat maps and family records. Chapman's 1881 county history gives the city of Goshen its own long chapter.

name: St. Joseph
lede: St. Joseph sits on the bluff where the St. Joseph River meets Lake Michigan. La Salle built Fort Miami near here in the winter of 1679, and William Burnett kept a trading post at the river mouth from about 1780. Calvin Britain and Augustus Newell took up land in 1829, and the village they laid out was first called Newburyport. It was incorporated as St. Joseph in 1834, became a city in 1891, and in 1894 took the county seat from Berrien Springs.
facts: Founded
land claimed by Calvin Britain and Augustus B. Newell, 1829; post office 1831, with Britain as first postmaster; village of St. Joseph incorporated March 7, 1834; city, June 5, 1891
Name
for the river. Ellis's 1880 county history records that the place was first called Newburyport, and the probate court dated its papers "Newburyport (St. Joseph)" until 1837
The fruit port
Ellis tells of seedling peaches from B. C. Hoyt's garden shipped across the lake to Chicago in 1839; once the timber trade waned, fruit became the port's chief export
Industry
in 1911 the Upton brothers began making electric washing machines in St. Joseph; the business became the Whirlpool Corporation
County seat
yes, of Berrien County since 1894, when a county vote moved the seat from Berrien Springs
where: St. Joseph is the county seat, but Berrien County's older vital records are kept by the County Records Department at 2100 E. Empire Ave., Benton Township: births and deaths from 1867, marriages from 1831; birth records over 100 years old are open. The Maud Preston Palenske Memorial Library in St. Joseph keeps a local history room. The Heritage Museum & Cultural Center on Main Street has archival collections and a research library. The St. Joseph Traveler, Herald and Herald-Press run from 1859 into the 1970s, much of it digitized on Newspapers.com and NewspaperArchive (subscription). Ellis's History of Berrien and Van Buren Counties (1880) gives the town a full chapter.

name: Benton Harbor
lede: Benton Harbor was dug into being. In 1859 Sterne Brunson, Charles Hull and Henry C. Morton planned a canal from the east bank of the St. Joseph River across the marsh, and the first ship canal, 25 feet wide, was finished in 1862. The village laid out beside it in 1860 was called Brunson's Harbor; in 1865 it took the name of Benton Township instead. It was chartered as a village in 1869 and became a city in 1891, the busy fruit-shipping twin of St. Joseph across the river.
facts: Founded
village laid out, 1860; ship canal finished, 1862, and widened in 1868; village charter approved April 3, 1869; city, 1891
Name

first Brunson's Harbor, at Sterne Brunson's request; renamed in 1865 for Benton Township, which had been named in 1837 for Senator Thomas Hart Benton of Missouri, a friend of Michigan's admission as a state
The canal

Ellis's 1880 history prints a Centennial address of July 4, 1876, telling how a canal was talked of in 1834 and revived in 1859, and how Martin Green was hired to dig it; the canal and the railroad pulled the district's trade to the Harbor
The oldest house
Eleazar Morton and his son Henry built the Morton House in 1849; four generations of Mortons lived there until 1936, and it is now the city's history museum
Fruit

by 1880 Ellis called the village the market-town for most of the people of the district; the old fruit market in the "flats" stood until urban renewal in 1967, and the market now trades in Benton Township
County seat
no; the county seat of Berrien County is St. Joseph, across the river
where: Berrien County's older vital records are kept by the County Records Department at 2100 E. Empire Ave., Benton Township: births and deaths from 1867, marriages from 1831. The Morton House Museum, 501 Territorial Road, calls itself the home of Benton Harbor history. The Palladium, in its many forms, runs from 1868 to the present; long runs are digitized on Newspapers.com and NewspaperArchive (subscription). The History Center at Courthouse Square, 313 N. Cass St., Berrien Springs, keeps a research library for the whole county. Ellis's History of Berrien and Van Buren Counties (1880) covers the village under Benton Township.

name: Buchanan
lede: Buchanan grew on McCoy's Creek, which drops about sixty feet on its way to the St. Joseph River and once turned more than a dozen mills. Charles Cowles settled there and built a sawmill in 1833, and the mill man John Hamilton platted the village in 1842. The Michigan Central Railroad came through in 1849, and the village was incorporated in 1858. In 1904 the town talked a Chicago firm into moving here; renamed Clark Equipment in 1916, it made axles and forklift trucks and kept Buchanan at work for decades.
facts: Founded
first settled by Charles Cowles, 1833; township organized 1837; village platted by John Hamilton, 1842; incorporated as a village, 1858
Name

for James Buchanan of Pennsylvania, later the fifteenth president; Ellis's 1880 history says simply, "The town derived its name from James Buchanan" — the township, organized in 1837, and the village after it
Mills
about thirteen water mills stood on McCoy's Creek in the 1800s; Pears Mill, built as a flour mill in 1857–58, is the only one left
A fire
in 1862 fire leveled much of the downtown; merchants rebuilt in brick, and the three-story Union Block, with its upstairs hall, went up in 1863
Industry
the George R. Rich Manufacturing Company came from Chicago in 1904–05 with about thirty men; as Clark Equipment it employed nearly 1,300 by 1929 and became a Fortune 500 company
County seat
no; the county seat of Berrien County is St. Joseph
where: The Buchanan District Library, 128 E. Front St., has scanned and put online almost every issue of the Berrien County Record and Buchanan Record it holds, more than 5,800 issues from 1868 to 1998, with smaller runs of the town's other papers. Berrien County's older vital records are kept by the County Records Department at 2100 E. Empire Ave., Benton Township: births and deaths from 1867, marriages from 1831. The History Center at Courthouse Square, 313 N. Cass St., Berrien Springs, keeps a research library for the county. Ellis's 1880 History of Berrien and Van Buren Counties covers the village under Buchanan Township.

name: Berrien Springs
lede: Berrien Springs stands on Wolf's Prairie, a tract of about a thousand acres in a bend of the St. Joseph River. John Pike made the first settlement there in 1829, and the village of Berrien was laid out in 1831. In 1837 the legislature made it the county seat, and the courthouse finished in 1839 still stands on its square, the oldest in Michigan. The seat moved to St. Joseph in 1894, and the old square is now the county's history center.
facts: Founded
first settlement by John Pike at Wolf's Prairie, 1829; village of Berrien platted, 1831; post office renamed Berrien Springs, 1836
Name
for the county, which was named for John M. Berrien of Georgia, attorney general under President Jackson, 1829–31; "Springs" was added for the mineral springs found near the village
County seat
from 1837, by an act of February 25 effective May 1, until April 1894, when a county vote moved the seat to St. Joseph; the proprietors gave the county four village lots for its buildings
The courthouse
built by Gilbert B. Avery and opened in April 1839 at a cost of about $2,500; it is called Michigan's oldest courthouse
The first fair
the county agricultural society met at the courthouse in February 1850, and the first county fair was held at Berrien Springs in 1851
Pickles
the village once called itself the Christmas pickle capital of the world, and its pickle festival was revived in 2021
where: The History Center at Courthouse Square, 313 N. Cass St., run by the Berrien County Historical Association in the old county buildings, opened a research library in the upper floors of the restored sheriff's residence after 2021. Berrien County's older vital records are kept by the County Records Department at 2100 E. Empire Ave., Benton Township: births and deaths from 1867, marriages from 1831. Ellis's History of Berrien and Van Buren Counties (1880) tells the village's story under Oronoko Township, with the names of the first settlers on Wolf's Prairie.

landmarks.address: Bounded by Cass, Kimmel, Madison and Union Streets, Berrien Springs

name: Three Rivers
lede: Three Rivers takes its name from where it stands: the place where the Rocky and the Portage rivers flow into the St. Joseph. Cutler's 1911 county history traces a settlement here back to George Buck's village of about 1830, and the village of Three Rivers grew up through the early 1830s, with its first frame house in 1834. It was incorporated as a city in 1895.
facts: Founded
settled about 1830 ("George Buck's village"); the village of Three Rivers grew up between 1830 and 1836; city, 1895
Name
for the meeting of three rivers, the St. Joseph, the Rocky and the Portage, which Cutler (1911) says "gives the city its name"
First building
Cutler records the first frame house in the town in 1834
Neighbors
a rival village, Eschol, was laid out just outside Three Rivers about 1838–40
County seat
no; the county seat of St. Joseph County, Michigan, is Centreville
where: St. Joseph County, Michigan, keeps its records at Centreville, the county seat. Everts's History of St. Joseph County (1877) and Cutler's two-volume History of St. Joseph County (1911) both give Three Rivers long chapters; both are free on the Internet Archive.
